Technical analysis produces multiple indicators that help with reading the market data. The analysis methods used are Moving Averages (MA), Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), Bollinger Bands (BB), Relative Strength Index (RSI) and Fibonacci Retracement. 

Moving Averages uses the average of a selected number of past prices and is used to identify short/longer trend direction and potential change of trend. Its score is calculated by using a scale of 0-10, with 10 indicating a strong buy and 0 a strong sell. The score is based on the direction of the average price relative to the latest closing price. A score of 5 or more indicates a buy signal, while a score of 2 or less indicates a sell signal.

Moving Average Convergence Divergence measures the relationship between two moving averages and is used to identify potential trading opportunities. MACD histogram is calculated by subtracting the 26-period EMA from a 12-period EMA. The histogram is usually used to identify divergences. A positive histogram above 0 indicates a bullish trend, while a negative histogram below 0 indicates a bearish trend. The signal line is a 9 period EMA of the MACD line and is used to confirm the trading signals. A buy signal is generated when the MACD line crosses above the signal line, while a sell signal is generated when the MACD line crosses below the signal line. MACD is a trend-following indicator and should be used in conjunction with other technical indicators. 

Bollinger Bands are volatility indicators that use a moving average and standard deviations to identify overbought and oversold conditions. A Bollinger Band squeeze occurs when the Bollinger Bands narrow, indicating a period of low volatility. A breakout from a Bollinger Band squeeze can be a sign of a new trend. Bollinger Bands are a versatile tool that can be used to identify trends, overbought and oversold conditions, and potential trading opportunities.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum indicator that measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate overbought or oversold conditions in an asset. RSI is calculated using a formula that takes into account the average gain and loss over a specified period of time. The most common period used is 14. RSI values range from 0 to 100, with a reading above 70 indicating that an asset is overbought and a reading below 30 indicating that an asset is oversold. RSI can be used to generate trading signals by looking for divergences between the RSI and the price of an asset.

The Fibonacci Retracement is a technical analysis tool that identifies potential areas of support and resistance. Fibonacci retracement levels are calculated by taking two significant price points and dividing the vertical distance between them into Fibonacci ratios. The most common Fibonacci ratios are 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 78.6%. Fibonacci retracement levels can be used to identify potential areas to buy or sell an asset.
